label: Re-input of first token p at copy step L+1 (long sequences)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase at the step right after the first output (recall_idx == 1, step L+1), when the fed-back input is the first original token and that token is p. 99.7% of activation mass has in_tok = p (equivalently first_tok = p). It requires L >= 6: almost nothing at L=5 and nothing at L <= 4. Magnitude increases with L (mass shares 7% at L=6, 22% at L=7, 32% at L=8, 39% at L=9), and the smallest activations come from L=6 sequences. Many false positives at L=6 are inactive. It does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, at any other recall position, or on p at later copy steps. Missed activations are very weak (<0.06 of max), at recall_idx 1 with other first tokens such as 3, 2 and t.

issues: All factual claims hold on the dev profile. Phase: 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase and 0 activations occur in the original or delimiter phases. recall_idx: 100% of mass is at recall_idx==1 and 0 activations occur at any other recall_idx. in_tok=p: 99.7% of mass. Mass share by L: 0.070, 0.224, 0.320 and 0.387 for L=6..9. Activation counts: 11 at L=5 and 0 at L<=4.
Mean magnitude does rise with L: L=6 has 2463 activations but only 7% of the mass, while L=9 has 3069 activations and 39% of the mass.

On the test split the false positives are almost all at L=6: 242 of the 243 come from L==6. With L==6 alone the predicate's precision is 0.913, while with L>=7 it is 0.9999. This is a weak boundary effect at the shortest length and the explanation already mentions it.

Minor systematic sub-pattern inside the L=6 false positives: when p appears again at position 2 (orig(2)==p), precision is only 0.376 on about 93 predicted steps, against 0.932 otherwise. Excluding that case lifts test F1 only slightly, from 0.976 to 0.977, so it is not a meaningful gap.
The test-split misses (295 steps, 0.2% of the mass) are all very weak (<=0.09 of max) and occur at recall_idx 1 with other first tokens (3, g, t, k). This is scattered noise.

The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate. One note: the predicate uses in_tok and the explanation says this is equivalent to first_tok, which is true only when the model copies correctly. That is fine here.
